HEADLINE ON PAGE: Exiled opposition leader Maria Corina Machado returns to Venezuela
(The URL slug says "announces her return"; the live headline says "returns". The headline was upgraded. Use "returns".)
STANDFIRST: "Nobel peace prize winner's return after almost a year in exile is unlikely to please interim president Delcy Rodriguez"

IS SHE PHYSICALLY IN THE COUNTRY? YES, ON THE GUARDIAN'S ACCOUNT
- "It was not immediately clear how Machado, 59, had managed to return to Venezuela but footage on social media showed she was in Barquisimeto, the capital of Lara state, which is about 220 miles west of the capital, Caracas."
- "Images showed her surrounded by supporters holding mobile phones in a church called the Sanctuary of the Divine Shepherdess."
- The Guardian hedges the MECHANISM of her return, not the FACT of it. Her location is sourced to footage; the BBC independently reports she was photographed at Mass in Lara state. No detention reported by either.

HARD FACTS AND FIGURES
- Machado is 59.
- She left Venezuela last December, "a few weeks before Maduro's capture", to collect the Nobel peace prize. The Guardian says "almost a year in exile"; the BBC says "over 10 months". FIGURE CONFLICT, do not average: Guardian "almost a year", BBC "over 10 months".
- Barquisimeto is about 220 miles west of Caracas.
- "in recent months has reportedly made more than half a dozen failed attempts to return home, including after the devastating earthquake that hit the northern coast in June." (BBC says an adviser put it at seven attempts in the weeks before September. Both as published.)
- She gave Donald Trump her 2025 Nobel peace prize medal.
- Her movement "is widely believed to have beaten Maduro in the 2024 presidential election".

THE US POSITION — THIS IS THE STORY'S EDGE
- The Guardian reports that the US "had reportedly opposed Machado's return, believing her presence would complicate the cosy relationship it has struck up with the interim president, Delcy Rodriguez, since abducting her former boss, Nicolas Maduro, in January." REPORTEDLY — not confirmed, no named official. Flag as a report if used.
- "Machado and Rodriguez are arch political rivals."
- "Instead the US president embraced Rodriguez, Maduro's vice-president, who now governs a country widely seen as a US protectorate."

NAMED QUOTES
- Maria Corina Machado on X on Sunday lunchtime: "I'm here. With you." (BBC renders the same post as "I am here. With you." Trivial wording difference between outlets; prefer the BBC's or quote neither verbatim.)
- Edmundo Gonzalez, Machado ally, in exile: "Venezuela! I am thrilled to announce to you that our leader, my dear Maria Corina, is on Venezuelan soil." And: "Today is a very important day for Venezuelans. Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process!" He added he too would soon return.
- DONALD TRUMP, US President, asked by reporters on Sunday about her return: "I don't know anything about it, but I think she's a very nice woman. She gave me her Nobel prize, so how can I say anything else?"
- Trump: "I hope she's safe. She's a very nice woman. But we're doing very well in Venezuela."
  THIS TRUMP REACTION IS GUARDIAN-ONLY among the sources I reached. The BBC piece does not carry it. It is the sharpest line available: the US president saying he knows nothing about the return of the opposition leader whose Nobel medal he holds.

NO STATEMENT FROM DELCY RODRIGUEZ OR THE VENEZUELAN GOVERNMENT. NO SECURITY RESPONSE REPORTED. NO CROWD ESTIMATE GIVEN BY EITHER OUTLET.
